title: Fish Pie
subtitle: Smoked haddock, salmon, and prawns under mashed potato
excerpt: A classic British fish pie with a mixture of smoked haddock, salmon, and prawns in a parsley cream sauce, topped with buttery mashed potato. Made ahead and baked when needed.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish pie is a British comfort food tradition with documented roots in the nineteenth century, though fish under a mash or pastry crust is an older idea. The combination of smoked and fresh fish in a white or cream sauce under mashed potato became the standard domestic version during the mid-twentieth century. It is a practical dish for using several types of fish together and is deeply associated with British home cooking.

content.text: Fish pie needs the sauce to be slightly thicker than a normal white sauce, because the fish releases more liquid as it bakes. Poach the fish briefly in milk first, use that milk for the sauce, and the flavour will be much better than using plain milk. The prawns go in raw so they do not overcook in the oven. Hard-boiled eggs are optional but traditional.

Poach the smoked haddock: put in a pan with the milk and bay leaves. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and cook for 6 minutes. Remove the fish and flake into large pieces, discarding the skin and bones. Strain the milk and set aside. Discard the bay leaves.

Make the sauce: melt 60 g butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm fish-poaching milk. Stir until thick. Add the cream, parsley, and lemon juice. Season. The sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon heavily.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the remaining 40 g butter. Season well.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Arrange the flaked haddock, smoked salmon chunks, raw prawns, and boiled egg quarters in the baking dish. Pour the sauce over everything and stir gently to coat. Spread the mash over the top and scatter with parmesan.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
